doctrines.conclusion_template: Physical security threats to the McWilliams Bloodline require layered defense: perimeter hardening, access control, surveillance systems, and personal security protocols. The Permian Basin operating environment presents unique physical risks including remote site vulnerability, equipment theft, and confrontation with hostile parties.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Physical threat assessment follows the CARVER matrix methodology: Criticality (how vital is the target), Accessibility (how easy to reach), Recuperability (how quickly can target recover), Vulnerability (how susceptible to attack), Effect (what is the broader impact), Recognizability (how identifiable is the target). Each factor scored 1-10. Combined score determines threat priority.

doctrines.conclusion_template: Cybersecurity threats to ECHO PRIME infrastructure require continuous monitoring across all attack surfaces: network perimeter, endpoints, cloud services (Cloudflare Workers, R2, D1), credentials, and social engineering vectors. The NIST Cybersecurity Framework provides the authoritative structure.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Cyber threat assessment uses the MITRE ATT&CK framework to map adversary TTPs. Primary attack surface includes 26 Cloudflare Workers, 10 R2 buckets, 10 D1 databases, 20 KV namespaces, Vercel deployments, GitHub repositories, and local infrastructure. Score likelihood and impact per attack vector.
threat_indicators: API key usage from unexpected geos

doctrines.conclusion_template: Financial threats encompass unauthorized transactions, invoice fraud, identity theft, embezzlement, and market manipulation. Detection relies on pattern analysis: transaction velocity, amount anomalies, new payee verification, and geographic inconsistencies.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Multi-layered detection: (1) Transaction monitoring for 2σ amount deviations, (2) Velocity analysis for unusual frequency, (3) New payee verification, (4) Geographic analysis, (5) Pattern matching against known fraud (invoice splitting, round numbers, weekend transactions). O&G specific: phantom invoices, royalty underpayment, JIB manipulation.
threat_indicators: New payee not in approved list

doctrines.conclusion_template: Legal threats include civil litigation, regulatory actions, contract disputes, mineral rights challenges, environmental compliance, and employment claims. Proactive legal posture requires continuous monitoring of pending actions and statute of limitations tracking.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Evaluate: (1) Active litigation stage/counsel quality/likely outcomes, (2) Regulatory exposure from pending changes, (3) Contract risks at renewal, (4) Title risks from chain gaps, (5) Employment risks from FLSA compliance. Assess probability of adverse outcome, financial exposure, timeline, and available defenses.

doctrines.conclusion_template: Reputation threats can destroy business relationships, credit access, and community standing faster than any other domain. Monitoring requires continuous scanning of social media, news outlets, court records, and industry forums.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: PEST + Stakeholder model: Political alignment, Economic perceptions, Social sentiment, Technological presence integrity. For each stakeholder group (employees, partners, regulators, community, media), assess current sentiment, trend direction, and trigger events. Weight by stakeholder influence.
mitigation_templates: Media contact list for rapid response

doctrines.conclusion_template: Insider threats are the most damaging and hardest-to-detect domain. Detection relies on behavioral analytics: access pattern deviations, data movement anomalies, and psychosocial indicators of disaffection.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: CERT Insider Threat Model: (1) Technical — unusual access times, bulk downloads, unauthorized storage, (2) Behavioral — dissatisfaction, conflicts, financial stress, (3) Organizational — performance issues, denied promotion, (4) Contextual — critical system access, security gap knowledge. Score combines anomaly detection with human factors.
primary_authority: CERT Insider Threat Best Practices (CMU SEI)
mitigation_templates: Encryption at rest and in transit

doctrines.conclusion_template: Supply chain threats affect physical operations (equipment, materials) and digital infrastructure (npm/pip packages, cloud providers, SaaS tools). SolarWinds and Log4j demonstrated catastrophic cascade potential.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Evaluate: (1) Criticality — operation dependency, (2) Substitutability — alternative lead time, (3) Visibility — security insight, (4) Geographic risk — disaster/sanctions exposure, (5) Financial health — bankruptcy risk. Digital: dependency depth, maintainer trust, vulnerability history, update frequency.
mitigation_templates: SOC2 Type II for SaaS vendors

doctrines.conclusion_template: Geopolitical risks include oil price volatility (OPEC+), US energy policy shifts, water rights conflicts in West Texas, environmental regulatory tightening, and international sanctions affecting supply chains. These directly impact royalty income, operational costs, and asset values.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Multi-factor model: (1) Oil price — OPEC+ decisions, shale growth, demand trends, SPR policy, (2) Regulatory — EPA methane, RRC rules, federal leasing, (3) Water — Ogallala depletion, disposal regulations, recycling mandates, (4) Infrastructure — pipeline capacity, export access, (5) Labor — skilled worker availability, immigration policy, wage inflation.

doctrines.conclusion_template: With 1,527 credentials in the Master Vault, credential compromise is high-probability, high-impact. Attack vectors include phishing, credential stuffing, session hijacking, and API key leakage in code repositories.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Enumerate all credential stores, assess exposure (age, complexity, reuse, breach presence), evaluate access scope per credential, check MFA coverage, verify rotation compliance. Priority: scope × exposure × MFA absence = risk.

doctrines.conclusion_template: Ransomware is the highest-impact cyber threat. ECHO PRIME's multi-drive architecture presents a large attack surface. Defense requires immutable backups, network segmentation, EDR, and a tested recovery plan.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Assess: (1) Attack surface — endpoints, drives, network shares, (2) Backup integrity — immutable/air-gapped?, (3) Detection capability for encryption patterns, (4) RTO from backup, (5) Business impact per hour of shutdown. R2 cloud backups provide off-site immutability; local drives are vulnerable if unsegmented.

doctrines.conclusion_template: Social engineering exploits human psychology. The Commander's public profile makes him a high-value target for spear phishing, BEC, and impersonation attacks.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Assess: (1) Target public information exposure, (2) Attack vectors (email, voice, SMS, physical), (3) Pretext scenarios (vendor payment change, exec impersonation, IT support), (4) Current defenses (DMARC/DKIM/SPF, training), (5) Historical incidents.

doctrines.conclusion_template: Environmental compliance threats include methane regulations, flaring restrictions, produced water disposal rules, groundwater contamination liability, and endangered species habitat. Non-compliance risks fines ($50K+/day), shutdowns, and criminal liability.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Assess: (1) Current requirements — EPA methane, TCEQ air, RRC flaring, UIC permits, (2) Pending changes — methane fee, WOTUS expansion, PFAS, (3) Compliance status — inspections, violations, corrective actions, (4) Financial exposure — max fines, remediation costs, (5) Community/NGO pressure.

doctrines.conclusion_template: DDoS attacks targeting ECHO PRIME's 26 Workers and web properties could disrupt operations. Cloudflare provides baseline L3/L4 protection, but L7 attacks and resource exhaustion require additional WAF rules.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Assess: (1) All public endpoints, (2) Cloudflare DDoS tier, (3) Worker request limits, (4) Cascading failure risk, (5) Recovery capability. Application-layer attacks bypass volumetric protection.

doctrines.conclusion_template: ECHO PRIME's codebase (53,841+ lines backbone, 427 engines, 37K+ tools) represents significant IP. Theft vectors include unauthorized repo access, insider copying, competitive intelligence, and reverse engineering.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Assess: (1) Proprietary asset inventory, (2) Access controls per asset, (3) Detection capability for unauthorized copying, (4) Legal protection (trade secrets, NDAs, copyright), (5) Competitive landscape and adversary capability.

doctrines.conclusion_template: Economic downturn threatens Bloodline assets through reduced oil demand/prices, tightened credit, counterparty default risk, real estate decline, and portfolio losses. Permian Basin operations are highly sensitive to oil price cycles.
doctrines.reasoning_framework: Assess: (1) Leading indicators — yield curve, PMI, unemployment, confidence, (2) Oil price sensitivity — breakeven vs WTI, hedge coverage, (3) Credit exposure — maturity schedule, rate sensitivity, covenants, (4) Counterparty risk — partner financial health, (5) Portfolio exposure — allocation, concentration, liquidity.
